statement: A three-degree system ending in the Master Mason degree was being worked in English lodges.
verification_notes: Prichard's exposure describes the third degree; no second independent source is recorded yet.

statement: The OT III materials contain a cosmological narrative centred on a figure named Xenu.
verification_notes: SRC-0010 and SRC-0011 are separate court files from unrelated cases and count as independent. SRC-0012 is not counted: the postings drew partly on court-filed material.

statement: Penalty gestures were removed from the endowment ceremony.
verification_notes: Only one source recorded so far; contemporary press reports would make it independently corroborated.

statement: Instruction begins with a puja chanted in Sanskrit by the teacher, at which the student makes offerings.
verification_notes: Based on the court's findings in Malnak v. Yogi.

statement: Śaṅkara's commentary on the Brahmasūtra holds that śūdras are not entitled to study the Veda.
verification_notes: Based on the commentary's own text.

statement: The Mishnah forbids expounding the account of the chariot even to one student, unless the student is a sage who understands on his own.
verification_notes: Based on the Mishnah's own text.

statement: The restricted women's knowledge about Hindmarsh Island was fabricated.
locators: SRC-0036: report of 19 December 1995; SRC-0037: paras 133, 199, 330
verification_notes: The Royal Commission (1995) concluded the whole of the women's business was a fabrication. The judgment records that Dr Kartinyeri did not give evidence to the Commission and that the contents of the sealed envelopes were not before it (para 133). In 2001 von Doussa J heard evidence from several Ngarrindjeri women supporting its genuineness (para 330) and was not satisfied, on the balance of probabilities, that it was fabricated or was not part of Aboriginal tradition (para 199). The two bodies are independent and heard different evidence. Checked against the judgment text on 2026-11-04.

statement: In the Entered Apprentice obligation the candidate promises not to write, print, carve or engrave the secrets, under a penalty of having his throat cut, his tongue taken from the roof of his mouth and his heart plucked out, these to be buried in the sea sands a cable's length from shore, and his body burnt and the ashes scattered.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04.

statement: In the Entered Apprentice obligation the candidate swears under a penalty of having his throat cut across, his tongue torn out by its roots and his body buried in the rough sands of the sea at low-water mark.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. Pagination is that of the Dick & Fitzgerald third edition as marked in the open transcription. Not counted as corroborating the 1730 wording: Duncan may draw on earlier exposures.

statement: The Master's Part tells how Hiram was killed by three Fellow-Crafts with a setting maul, setting tool and setting beadle, hidden under rubbish and then buried on the brow of a hill, and found fifteen days later by fifteen brethren when a shrub came away easily from the disturbed ground; a sprig of cassia was placed at the head of the grave.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04.

statement: The Entered Apprentice sign is made by drawing the four fingers of the right hand across the throat; the token is the ball of the thumb pressed on the first knuckle of the other's forefinger; the words Boaz and Jachin, the two pillars of Solomon's porch, are given by lettering them alternately.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. The OCR does not preserve page numbers for this part.

statement: The Master's word, Machbenah, said to mean 'the builder is smitten', is whispered in the ear while the two men stand on the Five Points of Fellowship: hand to hand, foot to foot, cheek to cheek, knee to knee and hand in back.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04.

statement: The pass-word of the Fellow Craft degree is Shibboleth and that of the Master Mason degree is Tubal Cain; the grand word of the Master Mason degree, Mah-Hah-Bone, is given in low breath on the Five Points of Fellowship.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. Pagination is that of the Dick & Fitzgerald third edition as marked in the open transcription.

statement: Each student received a mantra individually at a puja held in a closed room with only the teacher present, having brought a white handkerchief, flowers and fruit, before a table holding a picture of Guru Dev; a week or two earlier the student signed a promise never to reveal the mantra.
verification_notes: Checked against the opinion text on CourtListener on 2026-11-04. These are the court's findings of undisputed fact.

statement: In the English translation of the puja chant supplied by the defendants, the teacher offers a series of items (a seat, ablution, cloth, sandalpaste, rice, a flower, incense, light, water, fruit, a betel leaf, a coconut and camphor light) to the lotus feet of Shri Guru Dev, bowing down after each.
verification_notes: Checked against the opinion text on CourtListener on 2026-11-04. Complements CLM-0004.

statement: The text names the five elements of worship as wine, meat, fish, parched grain and woman, ranks the kinds of each, says wine taken without the accompanying purificatory food is like poison, and holds that in the Kali age the fifth element should be only the practitioner's own wife.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. Read from the readable copy of the same 1913 edition (ia:dli.ernet.205077). The text treats the elements as literal substances, with restrictions.

statement: The password (synthema) of the Eleusinian initiates was a formula stating that the initiate had fasted, drunk the kykeon, taken something from the chest, handled it, and returned it by way of the basket to the chest.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. Butterworth renders kykeon as 'the draught' and notes an emendation that would change 'having done my task' to 'having tasted'. The source is hostile and its access to the rites is not established.

statement: The initiate advanced through seven grades, named Raven (corax), Occult (cryphius), Soldier (miles), Lion (leo), Persian (Perses), Runner of the Sun (heliodromus) and Father (pater), and on some occasions wore costume suited to the grade.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. Cumont bases the list on a letter of Jerome and on inscriptions; adding Jerome or the Felicissimus mithraeum mosaic at Ostia as sources would allow independent corroboration.

statement: In the Katsina initiation, held in the Marau kiva after a sand mosaic is laid, each child is set on the mosaic and whipped with yucca switches by one of two Ho Katsinas, nominally with four strokes; a sponsor may take some of the strokes in the child's place.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04.

statement: During the night dance that follows, the Powamu Katsinas dance unmasked, and the newly initiated children learn for the first time that the Katsinas are Hopi men.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. SRC-0035 (Stephen's First Mesa journal) is a candidate for independent corroboration.

statement: In the Neophyte obligation the candidate pledges to keep secret the Order, its name, its members' names and its proceedings, and to study the occult sciences, under a penalty of submitting to a deadly current of will set in motion by the chiefs that would strike him dead or paralysed as if by lightning; the Hiereus touches him with a sword as the penalty is spoken.
period: 1909 (as published); Golden Dawn practice of the 1890s
locators: No. II, 'The Temple of Solomon the King', pp. 253–254
verification_notes: Checked against a scan of The Equinox I(2) on 2026-11-04. Regardie's publication (SRC-0008), drawn from Stella Matutina papers rather than from Crowley, could corroborate it independently. A footnote says a later version, issued after the Horos scandal, softened the penalty wording.

statement: The hoodwinked candidate, bound with a rope, is led round the temple, barred by the Kerux, purified with water and consecrated with fire, and challenged by the Hiereus, before the hoodwink is removed and the three chief officers receive him with the words 'Khabs Am Pekht'; the Hiereus then entrusts the signs, grip, grand word and current password, which this account does not print.
verification_notes: Checked against a scan of The Equinox I(2) on 2026-11-04. Regardie's publication (SRC-0008), drawn from Stella Matutina papers rather than from Crowley, could corroborate it independently.

statement: After the admission the penalty is illustrated by a liquid that turns the colour of blood, and the ceremony closes with the words 'Khabs Am Pekht', 'Konx Om Pax' and 'Light in Extension'.
verification_notes: Checked against a scan of The Equinox I(2) on 2026-11-04. Regardie's publication (SRC-0008), drawn from Stella Matutina papers rather than from Crowley, could corroborate it independently.

statement: OT III describes Xenu, head of a Galactic Federation of 76 planets founded 95 million years ago, solving overpopulation by having people brought to Earth (called Teegeeack), placed by volcanoes and destroyed with hydrogen bombs; this is called Incident II. Xenu was later captured by loyal officers after a six-year battle and imprisoned in an electronic mountain trap.
locators: Hubbard's handwritten summary, as quoted by Spaink from Wakefield, The Road to Xenu, pp. 76–77; OT III p. 79
verification_notes: Checked on 2026-11-04 against Karin Spaink's quotations of the OT III pages filed in the Fishman case (SRC-0042), not the exhibit itself; locators are the filing's page numbers as she gives them.

statement: After the explosions the disembodied beings (thetans) were subjected to more than 36 days of implanted pictures, including God, the Devil, angels, space opera, trains, helicopters and scenes resembling modern England, collectively called R6, and were then taken to Hawaii or Las Palmas and packaged into clusters.
verification_notes: Checked on 2026-11-04 against Karin Spaink's quotations of the OT III pages filed in the Fishman case (SRC-0042), not the exhibit itself; locators are the filing's page numbers as she gives them.

statement: OT III also describes Incident I, set four quadrillion years ago at the start of the 'track', as a sequence of a loud snap, waves of light, a chariot, a cherub blowing a horn, further snaps and blackness.
verification_notes: Checked on 2026-11-04 against Karin Spaink's quotations of the OT III pages filed in the Fishman case (SRC-0042), not the exhibit itself; locators are the filing's page numbers as she gives them.

statement: The OT III procedure holds that a person's body is covered with clusters of these thetans (body thetans), which the student must audit one at a time through Incidents II and I; Hubbard warns that running the implant incorrectly can kill, for example by pneumonia, and says he himself went through it in December 1967.
locators: Hubbard's handwritten summary, as quoted by Spaink
verification_notes: Checked on 2026-11-04 against Karin Spaink's quotations of the OT III pages filed in the Fishman case (SRC-0042), not the exhibit itself; locators are the filing's page numbers as she gives them.

statement: The Druze books teach that God, who cannot be grasped by the senses or defined in words, has appeared to people at various times in human form, last as the Fatimid caliph al-Ḥākim bi-Amr Allāh at the start of the fifth century AH; that al-Ḥākim disappeared in 411 AH to test the faithful; and that he will return to triumph over his enemies.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. De Sacy's own summary of the Druze manuscripts in European libraries, not a translation of a single passage.

statement: They teach that the Universal Intelligence, God's first creation, appeared in the time of al-Ḥākim as Ḥamza ibn Aḥmad, through whom all other creatures were made and who is the sole channel of religious knowledge and the only mediator with God.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. De Sacy's own summary of the Druze manuscripts in European libraries, not a translation of a single passage.

statement: They teach that the number of human beings is always the same and that souls pass successively into different bodies; that believers must keep Ḥamza's seven commandments, chiefly truthfulness, charity towards fellow believers, renunciation of their former religion, and submission to God's will; and that all earlier religions were imperfect figures of the true one, whose ritual laws are allegories now abrogated.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text on 2026-11-04. De Sacy's own summary of the Druze manuscripts in European libraries, not a translation of a single passage.

statement: In the Neophyte grade the step is a short advance of the left foot; the signs are the Saluting Sign (leaning forward with both arms outstretched, as if groping for light), answered by the Sign of Silence (left forefinger on the lips); the grip is made foot to foot, the hands failing once to meet and then touching only the fingers; and the grand word Har-Par-Krat is whispered mouth to ear in syllables.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text of Volume Two (1938) on 2026-11-04. The ritual says the password changes every equinox, so that members who have left do not know it, and leaves it blank.

statement: The grand words and passwords of the Outer Order grades are: Zelator, Adonai ha-Aretz and Nun Heh (mystic number 55); Theoricus, Shaddai El Chai and Mem Heh (45); Practicus, Elohim Tzabaoth and Eloah (36). The password of the Portal grade is Paroketh, the veil of the Tabernacle, exchanged letter by letter.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text of Volume Two (1938) on 2026-11-04.

statement: The penalty in the Neophyte obligation was changed: the version printed in 1909 calls down a deadly current of will from the chiefs of the Order that would strike the oath-breaker dead or paralysed, while the Stella Matutina version printed in 1938 sets expulsion for perjury and submission, by the candidate's own consent, to a stream of power set in motion by the Order's Divine Guardians.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text of Volume Two (1938) on 2026-11-04. Also checked against The Equinox I(2). Each source attests one wording; the change itself is shown by comparing them, and the 1909 text's footnote also mentions a softened later wording.

statement: The Neophyte obligation also binds the candidate not to copy any manuscript without the Second Order's permission, to keep every ritual or lecture under the Order's label, not to let himself be put into a passive state in which an uninitiated person or power could take control of his words or actions, and not to use his knowledge for evil magic.
verification_notes: Checked against the Internet Archive text of Volume Two (1938) on 2026-11-04.

statement: Every elder receives a copy of Shepherd the Flock of God on appointment, and the Governing Body gives final approval to its contents.
verification_notes: Checked against the report on the Royal Commission's website on 2026-11-04. The Commission quotes the handbook; the handbook itself has not been read.

statement: The handbook places child sexual abuse under the scriptural offences of porneia, brazen or loose conduct, and gross uncleanness, and defines what each includes; its 1991 predecessor, Pay Attention to Yourselves and All the Flock, also had a lesser offence of uncleanness covering momentary touching.
verification_notes: Checked against the report on the Royal Commission's website on 2026-11-04. The Commission quotes the handbook; the handbook itself has not been read.

statement: Elders may take disciplinary action only on a confession, the testimony of two or three credible eyewitnesses to the same incident, or strong circumstantial evidence testified to by at least two witnesses (the two-witness rule). Without that, an accused person who denies the allegation continues to be viewed as innocent and the matter is left in Jehovah's hands.
verification_notes: Checked against the report on the Royal Commission's website on 2026-11-04. The Commission quotes the handbook; the handbook itself has not been read.

statement: The current handbook appears to require a complainant to make the allegation in the presence of the accused, and documents in evidence require witnesses to put their allegations to a judicial committee in the accused's presence unless that is impractical; the organisation's witnesses testified that survivors of child sexual abuse are no longer required to confront their abuser.
verification_notes: Checked against the report on the Royal Commission's website on 2026-11-04. The Commission quotes the handbook; the handbook itself has not been read.
